chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Asbat from Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person: at what time of the day does he use the siwak? He said, 'Whenever he wishes.' And reports have been narrated regarding the dislike of using the siwak with fresh (wet) wood.
ai.seo_question: When can a fasting person use the siwak during the day according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a fasting person may use the siwak at any hour of the day, emphasizing the general permissibility (*ibahah*) without restricting it to specific times like dawn or night. This ruling is often discussed alongside the secondary narration regarding *karahah* (dislike) of using fresh, wet wood, which some scholars interpret as a recommendation for using dried wood to avoid potential impurities or distraction, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both spiritual purity and physical cleanliness during fasting.
